standard.title: Certification Scheme for Occupational Health and Safety Person in Charge

notes: WHY module_kind = compliance, and why this may be the single largest module by seat count in the whole catalogue. Section 6.1 requires that 'All industries operating in the Emirate of Dubai shall appoint at least one (1) Certified OHS Person in Charge (PIC) for EACH WORK SHIFT AND EACH WORK LOCATION.' That is a quantified, countable, objectively checkable staffing rule — the strongest in Phase 5 — and it multiplies: an FM contractor running three shifts across twelve sites needs 36 certified PIC coverage slots, not one certified person. Nothing else in this corpus scales per shift per site. For a client like the one in view here, that is the difference between tracking a handful of certificates and tracking hundreds, and it is precisely the kind of obligation a spreadsheet loses. THE RELATIONSHIP TO S3 MUST NOT BE COLLAPSED. S2 and S3 were issued the same day and share their examination-conduct block, their two-year validity and their EIAC/ISO 17024 frame, but they certify DIFFERENT PEOPLE FOR DIFFERENT PURPOSES and this document says so three separate times: 'OHS Person in Charge (PIC) is not an OHS Practitioner and is not a substitute/replacement in work activities where the presence of a competent health and safety professional is required.' A client who has certified PICs has NOT thereby satisfied the S3 OHS Practitioner duty, and vice versa. The two modules are complementary, both are mandatory where they apply, and the resolver must never treat one as evidence for the other. Conversely there is a stated exemption in one direction only: the Department may exempt from PIC training and certification staff 'already registered as OHS Practitioner by Dubai Municipality' (section 7.4) — so a Practitioner may be excused the PIC certificate, but never the reverse. THREE SUBSTANTIVE DIFFERENCES FROM S3, all of which would be lost by assuming the siblings match. (1) Certification Bodies here are EXPRESSLY FORBIDDEN to provide training — 'Certification Bodies are not allowed to provide training to maintain the high level of impartiality of this certification scheme' (7.1). S3 contains no such separation, and GU131 positively requires the certification body to prepare training material. Three DM schemes, three different postures on the same conflict-of-interest question. (2) Training is MANDATORY here (the candidate must complete the approved course AND pass the examination), whereas GU131 explicitly makes training optional and the exam mandatory, and S3 has no training component at all. On a third-attempt failure the S2 candidate must repeat the whole process INCLUDING the training. (3) The failing inspection grades are 'D or F' here but 'D or E' in S3 — two documents issued the same day using different grade vocabularies for the same DM inspection regime. GU131 also says D or F. Do NOT normalise these into a single scale; record the grade as printed per scheme. AN ARITHMETIC CONTRADICTION IN ANNEX D, FLAGGED AND RESOLVED ON THE WEIGHT OF EVIDENCE. Annex D reads: 'Guided learning shall be provided a minimum total of twenty (20) hours within three (3) days which consists of: Twenty-three (23) hours on the delivery of training modules; and One (1) hour for examination.' The components sum to 24, not 20. Section 8.3.4 independently states 'The training time including the examination shall not be less than twenty-four (24) guided learning hours.' So 24 is corroborated twice — once by the component sum and once by the body text — and the '(20)' is a drafting error. 24 hours is encoded, with the conflict recorded on the limit itself rather than silently smoothed over. This is exactly the class of defect section 7.12 warns about, and had only Annex D been read the module would have shipped a training-duration check that was four hours short. A SECOND, UNRESOLVED CROSS-REFERENCE DEFECT: Annex D says examination questions shall place 'additional emphasis on modules 4 to 8' and that 'Module 6 to 8 shall be delivered using the following concept', but the training contents list in the same annex is an ELEVEN-ITEM UNNUMBERED BULLET LIST. There is no module numbering anywhere in the document, so 'modules 4 to 8' cannot be resolved to any content. This is the GU83 pattern from section 7.14 — cross-references that cannot be checked because the thing referenced was never numbered. Not relied on, and only DM can close it. EDITION: version V 1.0, issue date 1 November 2025. The cover prints 1/11/2025 numerically, which under rule 2 would be ambiguous with both components <= 12, but the page-2 history log prints '1st November 2025' in long form, settling day-first from inside the document; catalogue_editions.json records this at HIGH confidence and it is followed here. The general terms on p22 corroborate independently: 'The above requirements will be effective from the date of issuance November 2025.' Superseded issue date printed 'NEW' — a first edition. The source_url sits under /uploads/2025/12/, a month after issue. Code DM-HSD-S2 carries no GU number; guideline_no is null. WHAT COULD NOT BE OBTAINED: no list of recognised training companies or certified trainers, no fee schedule (fees are set by DM and providers may charge neither more nor less, but no figures appear), no renewal window length, and no statement of what happens between expiry and renewal.

competencies.requirement: A work supervisor appointed as OHS PIC as an ADDITIONAL responsibility alongside their existing job, responsible for overseeing safe execution of work and providing OHS awareness to employees under their supervision. Entry qualifications differ by sector and are stated as PREFERRED rather than absolute ('shall preferably possess'): Construction — Diploma in Civil, Mechanical or Electrical Engineering; Services — Diploma in Engineering or a relevant services profession, or a Bachelor's Degree in any discipline; Factories — Diploma in Engineering or relevant profession, or a Bachelor's degree in any discipline. All three sectors require total work and supervisory experience of at least 5 years, comprising 3 years in the relevant industry or similar company activity and 2 years of supervisory experience in a similar industry or activity. The candidate must then complete the DM-approved OHS Certification Course appropriate to the business activity AND pass the certification examination with an overall average of at least 60%, including at least 50% in the practical application (risk assessment) component. Who may be appointed: any work supervisor; the line manager or similar individual who is always present on site and has direct authority, control or supervision over employees; and — where the business entity is involved in different activities with FEWER THAN 150 EMPLOYEES — the employer or manager themselves shall be the OHS PIC.
competencies.issuing_body: Certification Body — a nationally or internationally reputed qualifications provider, UAE licensed, accredited by Emirates International Accreditation Center (EIAC) to ISO 17024 in coordination with Dubai Municipality. Note the Certification Body may NOT also provide the training.
competencies.renewal_requirement: Renew before the end of the second year of certification, by completing a ONE-DAY REFRESHER TRAINING of at least 8 hours approved by the Health and Safety Department, provided the sector-specific qualifications in section 6.3 are still met. Note this differs from the sibling S3 scheme, where renewal is by documentary CPD evidence or, failing that, an examination — here it is by attending a refresher course. THE CERTIFICATE IS ALSO INVALIDATED BY A SECTOR CHANGE: where the PIC changes sector employment (for example services to factories) within or upon completion of the certification validity, the issued certification becomes invalid and the full certification process must be followed for the new sector. Certification may additionally be cancelled with retraining and reassessment where the industry obtains an unsatisfactory company compliance grade (D or F) at routine DM inspection and further assessment confirms the PIC's inability.
competencies.trigger_event: appointment as OHS PIC for a work shift and work location; before the end of the second year of certification; and immediately on any change of employment sector
competencies.source_quote: Passing the Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) Certification Examination minimum overall mark of 60% conducted by the Certification Body under secure conditions (see Annex D). OHS Person in Charge (PIC) fulfilling all the scheme requirements as outlined in this guideline document and defined by the Accredited Certification Bodies shall receive a certificate valid for a period of two (2) years from the date of issuance. ... In circumstances wherein the OHS Person in Charge changes sector employment (e.g., from services to factories) within or upon completion of the certification validity, the issued certification will be invalid and shall follow the full certification process for the desired new sector as specified in Annex A.

competencies.requirement: Certified by an EIAC-accredited Certification Body to conduct this training. May be a full-time employee of an establishment provided they hold that certification. Must hold a Health and Safety qualification — a government-approved Diploma in Occupational Health and/or Safety, OR an international/national Diploma from NEBOSH, BSC, BCSP, Ofqual or NVQ, OR a government-approved Bachelor's degree in occupational health and safety on a 3 to 4 year curriculum — AND must have passed a Train the Trainer Program recognised by the Health and Safety Department and conducted by Certification Bodies. Experience: at least 5 years as an Occupational Health and Safety practitioner, including a minimum of 2 years' specific activity or sector experience, AND at least one or two years' training experience. Must have a clear understanding of the OHS PIC competence standards, the knowledge and experience to explain why those standards are required, and the training skills to deliver the programme effectively. Applications are assessed by the Certification Body on records of training qualifications delivered, a detailed resume of qualifications and experience, and ATTENDEE FEEDBACK. The register of certified trainers is maintained by Certification Bodies with up-to-date records provided to the Health and Safety Department.
competencies.issuing_body: Certification Body accredited by Emirates International Accreditation Center (EIAC)
competencies.renewal_requirement: No validity period or renewal interval is stated for trainer certification. What is stated instead is an annual reporting duty — training details submitted to the certifying Certification Body by 31 December each year — plus unquantified Continuing Professional Development. Approval ends by suspension or withdrawal on non-compliance rather than by expiry: trainers and training centres not meeting the requirements are stopped from providing training without prior notice, and approval is suspended for poor delivery until full competency is demonstrated. Recorded null honestly: this is an activity duty, not a validity period.
competencies.source_quote: Trainer should have at least five (5) years of experience as Occupational Health and Safety practitioner including specific activity/sector experience of minimum two (2) years. AND At least one (1) or two (2) years' training experience. (p19) This scheme-related trainer shall be certified by a Certification Body accredited by Emirates International Accreditation Center (EIAC) to conduct training. (p18) Passed the Train the Trainer Program (recognized by Health and Safety Department) conducted by Certification Bodies. (p19)
competencies.note: AMBIGUITY IN THE TRAINING EXPERIENCE FIGURE, recorded not guessed: 'At least one (1) or two (2) years' training experience' offers two numbers with no rule for choosing between them and no condition attached to either. As printed this is not a usable threshold. It is flagged here and NOT encoded as a limit, per the section 7.12 'omit an ambiguous cell, never guess it' rule — encoding 1 would be lenient and 2 would be strict, and the document supports neither over the other.

competencies.requirement: Recognised by the Health and Safety Department, with recognition continuing unless revoked by the Department or surrendered by the company. Must employ at least ONE person with the knowledge, experience and skills meeting the criteria in this document. Must have adequate systems and resources — staff and, where appropriate, equipment, materials and software — to support delivery, with competent staff having access to appropriate training, guidance and support. Must have a NAMED POINT OF CONTACT for each course delivered. Must use only training materials approved by the Health and Safety Department, and must always adhere to the quality processes and procedures of the Certification Bodies and the Department. Conformity to relevant ISO standards such as ISO 29993:2017 is PREFERRED, not required.
competencies.issuing_body: DM Health and Safety Department (recognition); audited by Certification Bodies against criteria developed jointly with the Department
competencies.renewal_requirement: No validity period — recognition runs open-endedly 'unless the recognition is revoked earlier by Health and Safety Department or surrendered by the company'. That is an explicit statement that there is no expiry, which is different from an omission and is recorded as such.
competencies.source_quote: Training companies will be recognized by the Health and Safety Department unless the recognition is revoked earlier by Health and Safety Department or surrendered by the company. Training companies having confirmatory to relevant ISO standards (e.g., ISO 29993:2017) are preferred. Training Companies may gain recognition as training provider of OHS Person in Charge training, provided they employ at least one (1) person with the knowledge, experience and skills required to meet the criteria set out in this document.

competencies.requirement: A nationally or internationally reputed qualifications provider, UAE licensed, accredited by EIAC to ISO 17024 in coordination with Dubai Municipality. EXPRESSLY PROHIBITED FROM PROVIDING TRAINING, to maintain impartiality. Must provide DM-approved examination materials, training syllabus and related training material in Arabic and English and other common spoken languages defined by DM; decide the lesson plan based on training outcome; recommend pre-course work to trainers; decide maximum class size and space requirements; conduct examinations; take all certification decisions; announce results and issue certificates; obtain and consolidate trainee feedback; respond to enquiries and appeals about results; deal with malpractice; and take all necessary action on suspension or withdrawal of certification. Must design and develop criteria for AUDITING training providers and trainers in coordination with the Department, and carry out audits against those criteria. Must maintain a documented system to cancel the certification of any PIC found incompetent by the Department during inspection. Must have a named point of contact. Must formally notify the Department where trainers or training companies fail to comply.
competencies.issuing_body: Emirates International Accreditation Center (EIAC) accreditation to ISO 17024, in coordination with Dubai Municipality
competencies.renewal_requirement: No accreditation validity stated; accreditation ends on withdrawal by EIAC or cessation of operation. Recorded null honestly.
competencies.trigger_event: before offering OHS PIC certification and registration in Dubai
competencies.source_quote: Certification Bodies accredited by Emirates International Accreditation Center in coordination with Health and Safety Department can offer OHS Person in Charge (PIC) Certification and Registration in the Emirate of Dubai. Certification Bodies are not allowed to provide training to maintain the high level of impartiality of this certification scheme. The accreditation will be granted as per ISO 17024 Standard by the Emirates International Accreditation Center.

competencies.requirement: Diploma or bachelor's degree or higher in a relevant field; specific training in the certification process, standards and best practices for reviewing applications, undertaken through a certifying body or other professional development programme; 2 years' experience in a field such as education or technology.
competencies.issuing_body: Certification Body (internal appointment; criteria set by this scheme)
competencies.trigger_event: appointment as a certification application reviewer
competencies.source_quote: 7.7 Requirements for Certification Application Reviewers: Education: Diploma or bachelor's degree or higher in a relevant field is often required. Training: Specific training related to the certification process, standards, and best practices for reviewing applications. ... Experience(years): 2Years.

competencies.requirement: Bachelor's or master's degree or higher in a relevant field; specific training in Health and Safety advanced programmes, the certification process, standards and best practices, undertaken through recognised international accredited entities; 3 to 5 years' experience in a field such as education or Health and Safety.
competencies.issuing_body: Certification Body (internal appointment); training via recognised international accredited entities
competencies.source_quote: 7.8 Requirements for Examiners: Education: bachelor's or master's degree or higher in a relevant field is often required. ... Experience (years): 3 - 5 Years. Experience (field): This could include fields such as education, Health and Safety etc.

competencies.requirement: High School or Diploma or higher, and/or NEBOSH/IOSH approved invigilators are also accepted. Invigilator training must be undertaken through a certifying body or other development programme. Experience explicitly not compulsory, in years or in field. At least one invigilator per 20 candidates; must arrive ahead of time, supervise throughout the entire examination, remain alert, give whole attention to the examination and undertake no other activity — no acting as reader or writer for a candidate, no translation or interpretation. Must intervene on cheating, photographing or copying questionnaires, talking or disturbing others; serious incidents mean the examination is cancelled and the candidate removed after their answer sheets and materials are collected.
competencies.trigger_event: appointment to invigilate a certification examination
competencies.source_quote: 7.9 Requirements for Invigilators: Education: High School or Diploma or higher is often required and / or (NEBOSH/IOSH) Approved Invigilators also accepted. ... Experience (years): Not compulsory. Experience (field): Not compulsory. (p16) there should be at least one invigilator for every 20 candidates (p13)
competencies.note: Word-for-word identical to GU131's invigilator requirements, including the 'Not compulsory' phrasing. Note S3, the sibling scheme issued the same day, sets NO invigilator qualifications at all despite sharing the ratio and desk-spacing rules — so the reused DM block is not applied consistently even across simultaneous documents.

competencies.requirement: Comprehensive knowledge and experience of working with certification; specific training in Health and Safety, the certification process, standards and best practices through recognised international accredited entities; 3 to 5 years' experience in a field such as education or Health and Safety.
competencies.source_quote: 7.10 Requirements for certification decision-makers: Education: Comprehensive knowledge and experience in working with Certification. ... Experience (years): 3 - 5 Years.

competencies.role: Certification body technical committee / scheme review committee member
competencies.requirement: Comprehensive knowledge and experience of the certification process and scheme reviewing; specific training in Health and Safety, the certification process, standards and scheme assessing through recognised international accredited entities; above 5 years' experience as an expert or specialist in Health and Safety.
competencies.trigger_event: appointment to the technical or scheme review committee
competencies.source_quote: 7.11 Requirements for certification bodies' technical committee/scheme review Committee: ... Experience (years): Above 5 Years. Experience (field): This could include fields such as experts, specialists in Health and Safety etc.

limits.parameter_label: Certified OHS Persons in Charge required per work shift and work location
limits.display: at least one (1) Certified OHS Person in Charge (PIC) for each work shift and each work location
limits.qualifier_rule: Applies to ALL industries operating in the Emirate of Dubai — factories, construction, infrastructure and service sectors. The multiplier is shifts times locations, not a single headcount per organisation. The appointed PIC must always be PRESENT throughout the conduct of the work activity they supervise, which means the requirement is coverage, not merely employment: a certified PIC who is off site does not satisfy it for that shift.
limits.source_quote: All industries operating in the Emirate of Dubai shall appoint at least one (1) Certified OHS Person in Charge (PIC) for each work shift and each work location. (p8) The appointed OHS Person in Charge (PIC) must always be present throughout the conduct of the work activity that he/she is supervising. (p9)
limits.note: Inclusive minimum. THE MOST OPERATIONALLY DEMANDING REQUIREMENT IN PHASE 5 and the one that scales worst by hand — coverage must be demonstrated per shift per site, so the compliance question is a roster question, not a certificate-count question. A client with valid certificates can still be non-compliant on a night shift.

limits.parameter_label: Employee headcount below which the employer or manager must personally be the OHS PIC
limits.display: the employer/manager shall be the OHS PIC if the business entity or establishment is involved in different activities with less than 150 employees
limits.qualifier_rule: Applies where the business entity or establishment is involved in DIFFERENT ACTIVITIES and has fewer than 150 employees. In that case the duty attaches personally to the employer or manager rather than to a delegated supervisor.
limits.source_quote: Note: In addition to supervision of work, the employer/manager shall be the OHS PIC if the business entity or establishment is involved in different activities with less than 150 employees. Also, the line manager or similar individual who is always present in the work site and has direct authority, control or supervision over employees can be appointed as OHS Person in Charge (PIC).
limits.note: Exclusive upper bound by the 'less than' glyph, per rule 6. The qualifier 'involved in different activities' is undefined and does real work here — it is not clear whether a single-activity establishment under 150 employees falls under this rule or outside it, so the applicability test cannot be automated with confidence. Flagged rather than assumed.

limits.parameter_label: Validity of an OHS Person in Charge certificate
limits.display: valid for a period of two (2) years from the date of issuance
limits.qualifier_rule: Runs from the date of issuance. Renewal must be completed before the end of the second year, so the actionable date precedes the expiry date. The certificate is ALSO invalidated outright, before expiry, by a change of employment sector — so validity is not a pure function of dates and a status field is required alongside them.
limits.source_quote: OHS Person in Charge (PIC) fulfilling all the scheme requirements ... shall receive a certificate valid for a period of two (2) years from the date of issuance. (p14) Note: Issued certificate is valid for a period of two (2) years from the date of issuance. The OHS Person in Charge (PIC) shall undergo renewal of certification before the end of the second year of the certification validity (Annex A, p23)
limits.note: A genuine competency validity, not an examination interval. As with S3, the document states no renewal window length and no grace period in either direction.

limits.parameter_label: Overall pass mark, OHS PIC certification examination
limits.display: an overall average mark of at least sixty percent (60%)
limits.qualifier_rule: Necessary but not sufficient — must be achieved together with at least 50% in the practical application (risk assessment) component.
limits.source_quote: To pass the OHS Person in Charge Certification examination, the candidate must obtain an overall average mark of at least sixty percent (60%) provided that the candidate achieved a minimum of fifty percent (50%) mark in the practical application examination (risk assessment). (p30) Passing the Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) Certification Examination minimum overall mark of 60% conducted by the Certification Body under secure conditions (p14)
limits.note: Inclusive minimum. Same 60% headline as the sibling S3 scheme, but the gating is different: S3 gates on three of six theory elements at 50%, S2 gates on the single practical risk-assessment component at 50%.

limits.parameter_label: Minimum mark in the practical application (risk assessment) examination
limits.display: a minimum of fifty percent (50%) mark in the practical application examination (risk assessment)
limits.qualifier_rule: The practical component requires the candidate to complete a workplace risk assessment from a scenario developed by the Certification Body, delivered as a drawing or picture appropriate to the candidate's work sector, in a prescribed format (assessor name, date, work area, time, task assessed, hazard, who might be harmed, how, existing controls, risk rating as likelihood/severity/result, additional controls, new risk rating, action monitored by, review date, signature). Marked against criteria agreed between the Certification Bodies and the Health and Safety Department. Maximum 40 points.
limits.source_quote: provided that the candidate achieved a minimum of fifty percent (50%) mark in the practical application examination (risk assessment). (p30) Candidate is required to complete a workplace risk assessment through a given scenario developed by Certification Bodies that should be completed within 20 minutes. This part shall be marked as per agreed criteria between the Certification Bodies and Health and Safety Department. Maximum mark is 40 points. (p28-29)
limits.note: Inclusive minimum. Note the marking criteria are 'as agreed between the Certification Bodies and Health and Safety Department' and are NOT published in this document, so the practical component's standard cannot be independently verified from the guideline.

limits.parameter_label: Questions in the knowledge and comprehension examination component
limits.display: 30 questions in multiple choice or closed type (e.g. true or false, yes or no) formats; maximum mark 60 points; completed within 40 minutes
limits.qualifier_rule: Questions and answers may contain pictograms and should be understandable. Must cover all module subjects taken during the training with additional emphasis on 'modules 4 to 8' — a reference that cannot be resolved, since the training contents are an unnumbered list (see file notes). Questions must be appropriate to the level of training and to the candidate's work sector.
limits.source_quote: This examination contains 30 questions in multiple choice or closed type (e.g. true or false, yes or no) formats. Questions and answers may contain pictograms and should be understandable. This part should be completed within 40 minutes. The maximum mark is 60 points.
limits.note: An exact specification. The two components sum correctly: 60 points knowledge plus 40 points practical equals 100, and 40 minutes plus 20 minutes equals the one hour Annex D allots to examination. Both were checked — unlike the guided-hours figure in the same annex, these reconcile.

limits.parameter_label: Minimum guided learning hours for initial OHS PIC training, including examination
limits.display: shall not be less than twenty-four (24) guided learning hours, including the examination; delivered within three (3) days
limits.qualifier_rule: Comprises 23 hours delivering training modules plus 1 hour for examination. The trainer should consider expanding the hours where a review of participants reveals learning disabilities, language barriers or other factors inhibiting learning.
limits.source_quote: The training time including the examination shall not be less than twenty-four (24) guided learning hours. (section 8.3.4, p21) Guided learning shall be provided a minimum total of twenty (20) hours within three (3) days which consists of: Twenty-three (23) hours on the delivery of training modules; and One (1) hour for examination (Annex D, p26)
limits.note: INTERNAL CONTRADICTION IN THE SOURCE, RESOLVED ON WEIGHT OF EVIDENCE AND FLAGGED. Annex D's stated total of 20 hours contradicts its own components, which sum to 24 (23 + 1), and contradicts section 8.3.4, which independently states 24. Two independent corroborations of 24 against one bare assertion of 20, so 24 is encoded. Had only Annex D been read, this module would have shipped a training-duration check four hours short. Inclusive minimum by the 'not less than' glyph. Only DM can formally correct the annex.

limits.parameter_label: Minimum duration of the renewal refresher training
limits.display: a minimum total of eight (8) hours for one (1) day
limits.qualifier_rule: Interactive refresher syllabus developed by Certification Bodies covering the same learning modules as the initial course, appropriately designed for one-day delivery. Approved by the Health and Safety Department. Renewal is conditional on the sector-specific qualifications in section 6.3 still being met.
limits.source_quote: OHS Person in Charge (PIC) who will be undergoing renewal of certification before the end of the second year of the certification validity, shall complete a refresher training course approved by the Health and Safety Department. Certification bodies shall develop an interactive refresher training syllabus covering the same learning modules but appropriately designed to be delivered a minimum total of eight (8) hours for one (1) day. (p30) The certification renewal can be obtained by completing a one (1) day refresher training approved by the Health and Safety Department provided that the sector specific qualifications as stated in Section 6.3 of this document are met. (p14)
limits.note: Inclusive minimum. This figure is internally consistent across the two places it appears, unlike the initial training hours. Note that renewal here requires ATTENDANCE at a refresher, with no renewal examination mentioned — a materially lighter and more predictable renewal than the sibling S3 scheme.

limits.parameter_label: Minimum distance between trainees in a training room
limits.display: sufficient space between the trainees with a minimum distance of one (1) meter between two people
limits.qualifier_rule: Applies to the TRAINING room, and is distinct from the 1.25 m examination desk separation. Training rooms must be suitable and solely dedicated to that purpose, with adequate lighting and ventilation and seating suitable for trainee comfort, as quiet as possible and free from distracting activities. Restaurant dining areas and rooms hosting other activities must not be used. Certification Bodies and the Department shall immediately stop training conducted in unsuitable rooms.
limits.source_quote: There should be sufficient space between the trainees with a minimum distance of one (1) meter between two people.
limits.note: Inclusive minimum. Do not conflate with the examination desk spacing — different figure, different room, different activity, and a venue can satisfy one and fail the other.

limits.parameter_label: Minimum separation between candidate desks or computers at a certification examination
limits.display: not less than 1.25 meters apart (measured from the center of the desk/computer)
limits.qualifier_rule: Measured from the centre of the desk or computer. Where candidates share a large desk or the distance cannot be provided, multiple versions of the examination questionnaire shall be used.
limits.source_quote: Candidates should be seated at separate desks/computers (in case of computer-based examination) that should normally be placed at a distance of not less than 1.25 meters apart (measured from the center of the desk/computer).
limits.note: Inclusive minimum. Identical to GU131 and S3 — the reused DM examination-conduct block.

limits.parameter_label: Minimum invigilators per candidates at a certification examination
limits.display: at least one invigilator for every 20 candidates
limits.qualifier_rule: Applies to the Certification Body conducting the examination.
limits.source_quote: The Certification Body should appoint trained personnel to act as invigilators. Invigilators must arrive at the venue ahead of time and there should be at least one invigilator for every 20 candidates.
limits.note: Inclusive minimum. Identical to GU131 and S3.

limits.parameter_label: Minimum total work and supervisory experience for an OHS PIC candidate
limits.display: Total work and supervisory experience should be at least five (5) years: three (3) years in relevant industry or similar company activity, and two (2) years supervisory experience in similar industry or activity
limits.qualifier_rule: Applies across all three sectors (Construction, Services, Factories) — only the educational qualification differs by sector. The 5 years is composed of 3 years industry experience plus 2 years supervisory experience, so a candidate with 5 years of non-supervisory industry experience does not qualify.
limits.source_quote: Total work and supervisory experience should be at least five (5) years, that is: a. Three (3) years in relevant industry or similar company activity; and b. Two (2) years supervisory experience in similar industry or activity.
limits.note: Inclusive minimum. IMPORTANT SOFTENING, recorded not ignored: section 6.3 introduces the whole qualification table with 'shall PREFERABLY possess', which makes these entry requirements advisory rather than absolute — unlike S3, whose section 6 says 'shall possess' with no hedge. So a PIC candidate falling short of the qualification table is not automatically disqualified by the document's own wording, and the app must not treat this as a hard gate.

limits.parameter_label: Attempts permitted before the whole process including training must be repeated
limits.display: Candidate failing to clear examination in first and second attempts can retake the examination without repeating the training; candidates failing the third time shall repeat the whole process including the training
limits.qualifier_rule: Attempts one and two require only the registration, examination and assessment fees and do NOT require the training to be repeated. A third failure means repeating everything including the 24-hour course.
limits.source_quote: Candidate failing to clear examination in first and second attempts can retake the examination without repeating the training and by paying only registration, examination, and assessment fee (as defined by Dubai Municipality) each time. However, candidates failing the third time shall repeat the whole process including the training (see Annex A).
limits.note: Inclusive at three. The consequence is heavier than in the sibling S3 scheme, because the repeat includes 24 hours of training rather than an examination alone. No time limit is stated within which the three attempts must fall.

obligations.cadence_note: Two years from date of issuance, with renewal required BEFORE the end of the second year — so the due date precedes the expiry date. Renewal is by attending a DM-approved one-day refresher of at least 8 hours, conditional on the section 6.3 sector qualifications still being met; no renewal examination is required. No renewal window length and no grace period are stated in either direction. CRITICALLY, the certificate is also invalidated OUTSIDE the date logic by a change of employment sector, so an expiry date alone cannot determine validity and the app needs an explicit status.
obligations.trigger_event: approach of the end of the second year of certification; change of employment sector (invalidates immediately and requires the full process for the new sector); or an unsatisfactory company compliance grade (D or F) at routine DM inspection where further assessment confirms the PIC's inability
obligations.applies_to: Certified OHS Persons in Charge at all industries in the Emirate of Dubai
obligations.source_quote: OHS Person in Charge (PIC) shall renew the certification before the end of the second year of certification. The certification renewal can be obtained by completing a one (1) day refresher training approved by the Health and Safety Department provided that the sector specific qualifications as stated in Section 6.3 of this document are met. OHS Person in Charge (PIC) of industry obtaining an unsatisfactory company compliance (grade D or F) in the routine health and safety inspections of Dubai Municipality shall be considered for certificate cancellation, retraining and reassessment, if further assessment confirms his/her inability. (p14)

obligations.cadence_note: Standing coverage requirement with no interval — at least one Certified OHS PIC must be appointed for EACH work shift and EACH work location, and must be present throughout the work activity supervised. It becomes due on any new site, any new shift pattern, any vacancy, any certificate expiry, any sector change and any third-attempt examination failure. A state to be maintained, not a periodic task, and the hardest one in Phase 5 to maintain by hand because it scales with shifts times sites.
obligations.trigger_event: operation of any work shift at any work location; vacancy; certificate expiry; sector change; third-attempt failure
obligations.applies_to: All industries operating in the Emirate of Dubai — factories, construction, infrastructure and service sectors. The establishment must also ensure the PIC's registration with the Health and Safety Department is kept up to date, and all records of certified PICs for all industries are maintained with the Department.
obligations.source_quote: All industries operating in the Emirate of Dubai shall appoint at least one (1) Certified OHS Person in Charge (PIC) for each work shift and each work location. ... All records of certified OHS PIC for all types of industries shall be maintained with the Health and Safety Department. The business entity or establishment shall ensure that the registered OHS PIC to the Department is up to date. (p8-9)

obligations.cadence_note: DAILY, and this is the only daily obligation in the entire Phase 5 set. The PIC shall conduct daily pre-operational inspections to ensure the workplace is safe, and all inspections AND toolbox talks must be documented and presented to DM representatives when required. cadence_days is set to 1 accordingly. This is the operational heartbeat of the S2 module: two documented artefacts per shift per site, which is a very large volume of evidence for an FM contractor to produce and retain, and an obvious target for the app.
obligations.trigger_event: start of each work activity / each working day
obligations.applies_to: Certified OHS Persons in Charge — daily pre-operational workplace safety inspections and toolbox talks, both documented
obligations.source_quote: Conduct daily pre-operational inspections to ensure that the workplace is safe. Ensure that all inspections and toolbox talks are documented and presented to the official representatives of the Department when required. (p9)

obligations.cadence_note: No interval stated. Employees must be made fully aware of work hazards through toolbox talks AND trained BEFORE the start of work — a per-activity trigger rather than a cadence, though in practice it recurs with the daily toolbox talk above. No syllabus, duration, assessment or record retention period is specified for this employee-level awareness.
obligations.applies_to: All employees under the PIC's area of supervision — hazard awareness via toolbox talk and training before work starts
obligations.source_quote: Ensure that all employees are fully aware of work hazards (toolbox talk) and are trained before the start of work. (p9)

obligations.cadence_note: Event-driven with a stated but unquantified promptness requirement — non-compliances observed during DM OHS inspection must be rectified AND communicated to the Department 'on time', with no deadline defined. An honest null on the number: the duty and its urgency are stated, the deadline is not. This is a close-out tracking obligation and pairs naturally with the daily inspection record.
obligations.trigger_event: non-compliance observed during a DM OHS inspection
obligations.applies_to: Certified OHS Persons in Charge — rectification of observed non-compliances and communication of the rectification to the Department
obligations.source_quote: Monitor employee activities to ensure compliance with UAE and DM Health and Safety Regulations. Ensure that the non-compliances observed during DM OHS inspection are rectified and communicated to the Department on time. (p9)

obligations.cadence_note: Standing retain-and-produce duty, no interval and no stated retention period. A copy of the PIC certification and related health and safety trainings must be retained in the establishment and produced to official representatives of the Department when required. Note this says 'copy' where the sibling S3 scheme specifies 'soft copy' — a small but real difference between two documents issued the same day. Mapped to 'reporting' as the closest term in the closed vocabulary; the duty is retention and production on demand. Noted per rule 4.
obligations.trigger_event: request by official representatives of the DM Health and Safety Department
obligations.applies_to: Business entities and establishments — copy of each OHS PIC certification and related health and safety training records
obligations.source_quote: Copy of Certification of OHS PIC and related health and safety trainings shall be retained in the establishment and should be provided to the official representatives of the Department when required. (p9)

obligations.cadence_note: Annual but anchored to a fixed calendar date rather than an elapsed interval: trainer training details are due to the certifying Certification Body BY 31 DECEMBER each year, listing all training covered in that year plus all professional activities undertaken to improve the trainer's knowledge (other training programmes delivered, workshops, conferences, involvement with professional bodies, campaigns, journal articles). Those activities must be SEPARATE from the training and qualifications forming the basic trainer requirements and from routine trainer work. cadence_months is left null deliberately, because a 12-month rolling interval would drift off the fixed deadline. Note the recipient differs from GU131's equivalent clause, which sends the same report to the Health and Safety Department rather than to the Certification Body.
obligations.applies_to: Certified OHS PIC trainers — annual submission to the certifying Certification Body
obligations.source_quote: The details of training should be submitted to the certifying Certification Body by 31st of December each year and should list all the trainings covered in that year. The trainer shall also include all professional activities undertaken to improve his/her existing knowledge as a training provider ... Activities should be separate from the training and qualifications that are a part of the basic requirements to be a trainer and the routine work of the trainer. (p20)

obligations.cadence_note: Trainer Continuing Professional Development is required but entirely UNQUANTIFIED — no hours, no points, no minimum activities and no period. Honest null. Discharged in practice through the 31 December annual submission above.
obligations.applies_to: Certified OHS PIC trainers — maintenance of professional competence and enhancement of existing knowledge and skills in the related Health and Safety sector
obligations.source_quote: 8.2.4 Continuing Professional Development for Trainers. Trainers should strive to continually update and improve relevant knowledge of issues and developments in the related Health and Safety sector, and apply that knowledge for training and to ensure: Maintenance of professional competence; and Enhancement of existing knowledge and skills. (p19-20)

obligations.cadence_note: Event-driven with a stated lead time: the training course plan and session schedule are due to the Certification Body AT LEAST FIVE WORKING DAYS before the training is conducted. Subsequent changes are due 'without delay', which is not quantified. The plan must include training dates and timings, venue details, number of trainees, course language, examination time and any other details needed to register trainees. The provider must also confirm the training language and examination dates to trainees during registration.
obligations.trigger_event: at least 5 working days before a training course is conducted; and immediately on any change to the planned schedule
obligations.applies_to: Training providers submitting course plans and schedules to the Certification Body
obligations.source_quote: The training provider shall provide the training course plan and the schedule of training sessions to the Certification Body at least five (5) working days before the training is conducted. ... Any changes in the planned schedule shall be reported to the Certification Bodies without delay. (p20)

obligations.cadence_note: Standing access and notification duties, no cadence. Certification Bodies must give the Department access to records and documentation on certification, training provider, trainer, qualifications and audits, and give officials nominated by the Director access to examination question papers, scripts, marking records and associated documents. The candidate database maintained by both the training provider and the Certification Body must be accessible to Dubai Municipality. The register of certified trainers is maintained by Certification Bodies with up-to-date records provided to the Department. Certification Bodies must formally notify the Department where trainers or training companies fail to comply.
obligations.trigger_event: request by the Department or nominated officials; and on any trainer or training-company non-compliance
obligations.applies_to: Certification Bodies and training providers — certification, trainer and audit records; examination papers, scripts and marking records; candidate database (company name, main activity and sector, location, trade licence number; candidate job designation, age, gender, nationality, language skills, qualifications, experience); register of certified trainers
obligations.source_quote: Certification Bodies shall provide the Health and Safety Department with access to records and documentation relating to certification, training provider, trainer, qualifications and audits. (p11) The register of certified trainers shall be maintained by Certification Bodies and up to date records to be provided to the Health and Safety Department. (p18) The Certification Bodies should formally notify the Health and Safety Department if the trainers or training companies fail to comply with the requirements stipulated in this guideline document. (p12)

obligations.cadence_note: No frequency stated. Certification Bodies shall design and develop criteria for AUDITING training providers and trainers, in coordination with the Health and Safety Department, and carry out audits against those accepted criteria. The criteria themselves are not published in this document, and no audit interval is given. Honest null on both.
obligations.applies_to: Certification Bodies auditing training providers and trainers against jointly developed criteria
obligations.source_quote: Certification Bodies shall design and develop criteria for auditing training providers and trainers in coordination with the Health and Safety Department. Audits should be carried out based on the accepted criteria. (p11)

obligations.cadence_note: 'Periodically' with no period stated, for training material review; and no interval for the ISO 17024 scheme-effectiveness review. Examination materials, training syllabus and related material require DM approval before use (Annexes B and C), and that approval runs until content revision, revocation by the Department, cessation of the body's operation, or withdrawal of EIAC accreditation. BOTH annex notes say the approval certificate 'is valid for a specified period' AND NEVER SPECIFY IT — the same explicit-validity-with-no-number defect that appears in the sibling S3 scheme, here repeated twice.
obligations.trigger_event: content revision; revocation of approval; cessation of operation; withdrawal of EIAC accreditation; feedback from learners and trainers; change in H&S standards, regulations or best practices
obligations.applies_to: Certification Bodies — periodic review and update of training material in coordination with the Department, DM approval of examination and training materials, and review of scheme effectiveness per ISO 17024
obligations.source_quote: Regular Updates: Certification Bodies must review and update the training material periodically in coordination with the Health and Safety Department to ensure it remains aligned with changing Health and Safety standards, regulations, or best practices ... (p16) Note: Issued training material approval certificate is valid for a specified period unless there is content revision; or approval is revoked earlier by the Health and Safety Department; or the Certification Body cease its operation; or its accreditation is withdrawn by EIAC. (Annex C, p25)

obligations.cadence_note: No cadence stated for the PIC's standing duty to implement safety policies, procedures and risk control measures to prevent accidents and occupational illnesses in their area of supervision. Recorded because it is the substantive purpose of the role, and because the certification examination's practical component assesses exactly this capability — the candidate must complete a workplace risk assessment in a prescribed format. Note that where the establishment also employs an OHS Practitioner, 'the role of OHS PIC is limited' and the OHS Practitioner shall identify and document what the PIC's role is — so the scope of this obligation is itself set by another document's role-holder.
obligations.applies_to: Certified OHS Persons in Charge — implementation of safety policies, procedures and risk control measures within their area of supervision
obligations.source_quote: Implement safety policies, procedures, and risk control measures to prevent accidents and occupational illnesses under area of supervision. (p9) Note: In business establishments or entities that are required to employ full-time safety personnel (OHS Practitioners), the role of OHS PIC is limited. The OHS Practitioner shall identify and document the role of the OHS PIC. (p9)

obligations.cadence_note: Standing certificate-content requirement, no cadence. The certificate must bear: certification title, name of candidate, date of birth, designation or official job title, TYPE OF SECTOR (Construction, Factories, Service), Emirates ID number, signature of the issuing Certification Body, serial or control number, EIAC symbol, Dubai Municipality logo and Certification Body logo. Identical field list to the sibling S3 scheme. The sector field is not decorative — a sector change invalidates the certificate, so sector must be stored as a first-class attribute and compared against the holder's current employment, which section 4.4's certificates table has no column for.
obligations.trigger_event: successful completion of examination and assessment
obligations.applies_to: Certification Bodies issuing OHS PIC certificates
obligations.source_quote: Upon successful completion of examination and assessment, the Certification Body shall issue the Certificate bearing the following contents to the candidate: Certification title; Name of the candidate; Date of birth; Designation/official job title; Type of sector (Construction, Factories, Service); Emirates ID number; Signature of issuing Certification Body; Serial/control number of the certificate; EIAC symbol; Dubai Municipality logo; and Certification Body logo. (p21-22)

obligations.cadence_note: Standing training-environment requirements, no cadence, but enforceable by immediate stoppage. Training must be in rooms suitable and solely dedicated to that purpose, with adequate lighting and ventilation, seating suitable for trainee comfort, as quiet as possible and free from distracting activities; restaurant dining areas and rooms hosting other activities must not be used. Trainees must be at least 1 metre apart. Training providers shall group trainees working in the same sector type and similar work activities to maximise learning, and shall use animated presentations, scenario boards and other interactive tools. Certification Bodies and the Department shall stop immediately any training conducted in unsuitable rooms, and trainers or centres not meeting the requirements are stopped without prior notice; poor delivery suspends the trainer until full competency is demonstrated.
obligations.source_quote: Training should be conducted in rooms that are suitable and solely dedicated for that purpose. ... Restaurant dining areas and rooms that have other activities that could distract the trainees should not be used for training. (p21) Certification Bodies and Health and Safety Department shall stop immediately the trainings that are conducted in unsuitable training rooms. (p22) Trainers and Training centers that do not meet the requirements in this guideline document will be stopped from providing training without prior notice. (p22)
